Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine visit for acute gastroenteritis with 3 days of diarrhea, central abdominal pain, and vomiting; advised hydration, avoidance of antibiotics, and primary-care follow-up if worse or not improved.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for 3 days with abdominal pain and vomiting; frequent urgent toilet visits; unable to work due to urgency.
- Onset/duration/progression: Diarrhea started ~3 days ago; currently persistent with no clear improvement or worsening.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea; occasional vomiting (this morning); no definite blood in stool; appetite reduced; able to eat fruit; may be dehydrated.
- Negative findings: No fever reported; no chest pain; able to walk and talk.
- Past medical history: Asthma; uses inhaler; no known drug allergies (NKDA) noted.
- Medications: Inhaler (name, dose, route, frequency not documented).
- Social history / preventive care: Family history notable for father with bowel cancer (died ~10 years ago); no other details provided.
- Date of birth note: DOB provided as 01/01/1992; patient later stated age 48; conflict noted between statements.

Examination:
- Abdominal: mild tenderness on palpation.
- Other exam elements not documented.

Impression:
- Likely acute gastroenteritis (infectious) presenting with diarrhea, central abdominal pain, and vomiting; no evidence of gastrointestinal bleeding; no fever documented; antibiotics not indicated at this time.

Plan:
- Hydration: Encourage generous fluid intake and oral rehydration; monitor for fever.
- Avoid antibiotics: Not indicated; supportive care only.
- Activity: Stay home while symptomatic.
- Follow-up: If symptoms worsen or do not improve in 1–2 days, arrange in-person GP evaluation.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: Comprehensive meds reconciliation (complete list of all meds and doses), documented vitals, and detailed allergy confirmation beyond NKDA.
- Internal conflicts: Date of birth vs. stated age conflict (DOB 01/01/1992 vs age 48) noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some repetition and timing inconsistencies (e.g., DOB/age discrepancy) present; content sufficient to determine likely gastroenteritis and management plan.
